task:
Write Python 3 function solve(rows). Before the main rule, perform this audit scan in ORIGINAL zero-based order. For an integer row its weight is that integer. For a log-string row its weight is the signed integer between pipes. For a list row its weight is the sum of integer fields excluding booleans plus the lengths of all string fields. Start state at 11. Keep a row if (state + weight + original_index) modulo 13 is not 12, or if it is the last original row. After deciding, update state for EVERY row, including omitted rows: reset to 11 if its weight is zero; otherwise set state to (3*state + weight) modulo 13. Finally rotate the kept list LEFT by final_state modulo kept_length; empty stays empty. Then apply the following main rule: Rows [day, lifetime] use integer days; day zero is Monday. An item expires at day+lifetime. Move that expiry forward past Saturday/Sunday (remainders 5,6). Return the expiry days in input order.
Return the requested value, without printing. Inputs follow the types specified. Do not mutate the input. The execution environment permits built-ins and these standard-library modules: math, decimal, fractions, collections, itertools, functools, datetime, calendar, re, statistics, bisect, heapq, operator, string, typing, copy, json, ast, dataclasses, numbers and unicodedata. No file/network I/O is needed.
